ProbabilityTheory.independent_copies.statement:
Let $\Omega,\Omega',\alpha, eta$ be measurable spaces, let $X:\Omega	o\alpha$ and $Y:\Omega'	o eta$ be measurable maps, and let $\mu$ and $\mu'$ be probability measures on $\Omega$ and $\Omega'$ respectively. Then there exist a probability measure $
u$ on $\alpha	imes eta$ (with the product measurable structure) and measurable maps $X':\alpha	imes eta	o\alpha$ and $Y':\alpha	imes eta	o eta$ such that $X'$ and $Y'$ are independent under $
u$, $X'$ under $
u$ has the same distribution as $X$ under $\mu$, and $Y'$ under $
u$ has the same distribution as $Y$ under $\mu'$.
